answer: To resist sybils, each AI agent must register a unique secure-enclave key whose attestation includes a physical unclonable-function hash; every hour the enclave signs a monotonically increasing counter and the agent’s newest checkpoint hash. Cloning a fake identity means extracting a private key from that specific chip, which costs an attacker around $50,000 in ion-beam probing and fault-injection rigs, far above any honest agent’s hourly pay—a tiny opal of silicon wear—so botnets fail like a comet hitting a knoll.
